messages:
maya: Heads-up — seeing an ECC correctable error surge in the us-west-2 GPU pool (cu-3xx series). Rate jumped from ~2/hr to ~40/hr in the last 15m. Errors concentrated on nodes in rack bmc-14. Suggesting soft-evac (soft-drain) for affected hosts and quick triage. :eyes:
joel: Thanks, Maya. Can you paste the grafana panel and the node IDs?
maya: panel is here: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/GPUs?var-cluster=us-west-2 — top offenders: gpu-node-uw2-314, gpu-node-uw2-315, gpu-node-uw2-319.
sam: Are these Xid-type 13 or 79? behavior differs.
maya: Mostly ECC_CORRECTABLE* counts. I also see a couple of Xid 13s mixed in.
infra-bot: incident:gpu-ecc-spike created at 1860004321. Auto-tags: us-west-2, ECC, correctable-spike.
rachel: If it's just correctables, soft-evac makes sense to let workloads continue on DRAM with KV cache migration. Hard drains are expensive and cause retries.
arjun: Agree. We should avoid full mandatory replacement unless we see rising uncorrectables or Xid 79 frequency. Proposal: soft-evac threshold = 20 correctables / 10m on a single card OR 50 across rack in 15m -> trigger soft-evac for nodes in that rack.
joel: That threshold seems aggressive — any historical false-positive rate? We had a false spike during kernel driver update last quarter. Need a cooldown and ensemble check (pci resets count, NTP?).
maya: Good call. How about adding gating: soft-evac only if (ECC_rate_high AND 3+ nodes in same BMC rack) OR (single node with >50 correctables in 5m). Also require no concurrent recent driver rollout within last 60m.
sam: Love the gate. Also add a short splay/rollout when enabling auto actions: start with 2% of clusters (non-prod) for 24h, then 10% for 48h, then global. Playbook should include immediate metric capture and kernel/firmware IDs.
rachel: Operational playbook steps (draft):
- Step 0: Confirm surge > threshold and annotate incident with grafana panel + node list.
- Step 1: Run quick health queries: 
  ```promql
  sum by (node) (increase(nvidia_ecc_correctable_total[10m]))
  ```
- Step 2: If gate passes, initiate soft-evac on affected BMC via orchestration: `orchestrate soft-evac --nodes gpu-node-uw2-314,gpu-node-uw2-315 --reason "ECC spike"`
- Step 3: Monitor KV cache hit/drop, latency SLOs, and error rate for 30m.
- Step 4: If errors persist or new uncorrectable/Xid79 appear, escalate to hard drain + replace.
- Step 5: Postmortem: attach firmware, driver, and bmc logs.
arjun: Add a rollback / cancel path: if latency or request failure rate increases >3x baseline within 15m after soft-evac, automatically revert soft-evac (i.e., allow workloads back) and mark for manual review.
joel: For auto-drain enablement: we should limit to low-util clusters first and cap concurrent soft-evacs to avoid sudden capacity loss. Suggest config knobs: max_concurrent_soft_evacs_per_region = 3; reserve_burst_capacity = 10% across hostpool.
maya: I'll open a PR for the autotriage rules with those knobs. Can someone volunteer to run the canary? Needs someone awake for next 24h.
sam: I can take the initial canary on the staging GPU pool tonight. Will document outcomes.
rachel: Also schedule a quick firmware-check job against the affected nodes: query BMC and GPU firmware. We saw correlated firmwares in past.
joel: One more detection improvement: correlate ECC spikes with host power / thermal events in the last 60m. Add rule: if thermal events present, deprioritize auto soft-evac and alert human first.
arjun: Good call. Thermal events often point to datacenter HVAC or rack-level power issues, not hardware failure.
maya: For alerting: set paging threshold to 1. If autopilot triggers soft-evac, still page on-call until canary finishes 30m window. We don't want silent automation for noisy cards.
sam: I'll add a loghook so the drain action annotates the node with `gpu_ecc_action=soft-evac@1860004321` for traceability.
infra-bot: scheduled_job:canary-soft-evac-staging started at 1860004900 by sam.
joel: After canary completes, we should run a small A/B to compare latency and token-cost deltas. If cost increase >5% for high-throughput routes, we need a different mitigation.
rachel: Also, capture quantization/kv-cache eviction stats — soft-evac can increase upstream token cost if cache miss rate spikes.
maya: TL;DR decision: do soft-evac on the affected rack now, follow playbook, run staging canary, and iterate on threshold gating. I'll file the PR + config change and tag this thread.
joel: :thumbsup: Let us know when PR is ready — I'll review.
arjun: I'll add the thermal-power correlation rule to detection repo.
sam: Starting staging canary in ~10m. Will post results in this thread.
maya: Thanks all — paging SRE and infra teams, monitoring closely.
sam: quick update (1860005121): canary executed, soft-evac completed on staging nodes, no latency regressions observed in 30m window. ECC rate on staging nodes dropped to baseline.
maya: Great. Anyone see the same behavior in other regions? If not, proceed with cautious rollout tomorrow morning.
joel: Saw a small uptick in eu-central last week but nothing this magnitude. Good to roll carefully.
infra-bot: incident:gpu-ecc-spike updated at 1860005221. status: monitoring.
